subject: Aligning buffer plan for seasonal throughput spike — proposal & ops runbook
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@pivotretail.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning buffer plan for seasonal throughput spike — initial ask

Connor / Jordan,

Quick context: Pivot Retail sees a predictable ~2.5x increase in API volume every Nov–Dec due to Black Friday/Cyber Weekend traffic. We ran last year on your hosted API and the performance was solid, but this year our product team wants to lock in higher committed throughput so we can guarantee storefront SLAs.

Attached is a small usage extract (Pivot_Q3_usage_report.pdf) that shows our burst patterns. We want to discuss:
- A temporary commit uplift for Nov–Dec (targeting ~30% higher monthly commit vs current)
- A graduated rate-tier plan that reduces per-token costs as we hit thresholds
- Ops runbook for a canary week and throttling thresholds if we approach limits

Our procurement timeline is short — we need commercial terms by the end of next week to hit internal approvals. Can we get an outline of a proposal and an ops checklist by EOD Friday?

Phone available: +1 415 555 0128.

Thanks,
Sarah Patel
Director, Platform Engineering
Pivot Retail

Attachments: Pivot_Q3_usage_report.pdf (attachment)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@pivotretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning buffer plan for seasonal throughput spike — initial ask

Hi Sarah — thanks for the data and context. Short answer: we can support a temporary commit uplift and put a stepped-rate band in place for Nov–Dec. High-level proposal below; attaching a working amendment (Redwood_proposed_amendment_v2.pdf).

Proposal highlights:
- Commit uplift: +30% guaranteed monthly committed tokens for Nov and Dec (applies to hosted API plan)
- Temporary tiering: three usage bands during the uplift window with decreasing per-token rate above each threshold
- Burst buffer: enable a 20% burst pool for traffic spikes that exceeds commit; usage billed at the top-tier rate unless we hit agreed thresholds
- Canary week: full traffic routed to a canary pool for the first week of Nov with extra monitoring and rollback gates
- Billing/pricing: prorated amendment for Nov–Dec; post-Dec revert to baseline unless a renewal amendment is signed

Next steps / timeline:
1) I’ll share the amendment draft (attached) — legal will need ~72 hours for redlines.
2) Ops/infra (Jordan + Evelyn) will outline the canary runbook and rate-limit knobs by Friday EOD.
3) If procurement signs off, we’ll send a DocuSign link the following business day.

We can set a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the amendment and the canary plan. Proposed time: Thu 09/16 11:00am PT.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
Direct: +1 415 555 0190

Sarah / Connor — quick ops notes from my side after a run through with infra: 

Operational safeguards (short):
- Canary: route 10% of traffic to a canary pool with mirrored traffic for first 72 hours. If latency & error rate stay within SLAs we scale to full.
- Autoscaling: set soft and hard concurrency caps; soft caps trigger proactive scale while hard caps invoke graceful throttling with informative 429s and a retry-after header.
- KV/prefix caching: pre-warm caches for heavy prefixes (we’ll provide a pre-warm script to run 48h before canary).
- Rate tiers: implement stepped per-token pricing at thresholds 0–80%, 80–140%, >140% of committed usage during uplift window.

Commercial note: to help with your procurement run rate we can offer a one-month credit applied if you sign the uplift amendment by 22 Sep. That buys a little breathing room for approvals. Legal will want precise language around automatic revert on 01 Jan.

I’ll drop a short ops runbook and the pre-warm script link into the Drive folder by EOD Friday. If you want, we can also schedule an ops/quest call with your SREs.

—Jordan
